title: Bisect the Broken Board Status Check
description:
**SITUATION:**

Forgeboard has a **staging** environment — a pre-production copy of the product where QA signs off before anything reaches customers. Staging is updated from `main`. A **staging deploy** means rolling the current `main` tip into that pre-production environment, not into production.

Before each staging deploy, Ops runs `./check.sh` in `~/sprint-service`. That script is the Sprint Service health check: exit 0 means the service looks healthy, exit 1 means it does not. On today's `main` it prints FAIL and exits 1, so staging stays red and QA cannot sign off.

Tag `v1.0` is an earlier tip on this same history where `./check.sh` still passed. It is not a separate product you are shipping; it is the last commit Ops trusts as "check was green." Between v1.0 and today's `main`, about eighteen other commits landed.

Jordan skimmed the range while looking at the failing check. She is sure **exactly one** of those commits spilled the break — the rest look like unrelated noise — but she forgot to pin which commit it was before jumping to the next fire.

She handed you the follow-up: find that first bad commit's SHA so she can revert **just that change**. Git can binary-search the range for you; you do not need to read every subject.

Your identity (Ada Learner) is already configured. Start on `main` in `~/sprint-service`.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Confirm `./check.sh` fails on today's `main`, and that tag v1.0 is the last known good tip.
2. Binary-search between v1.0 (good) and main (bad) to find the first commit that makes `./check.sh` fail.
3. Write that commit's SHA to `~/answers/bad-commit`.
4. End the search so you are back on `main` with a clean working tree. Do not rewrite main.

hints: Start a search with `git bisect start`, mark today's tip bad (`git bisect bad`), mark `v1.0` good (`git bisect good v1.0`).
`git bisect run ./check.sh` lets Git check out midpoints and run the health check for you until it prints the first bad commit.
Save that SHA to `~/answers/bad-commit`, then `git bisect reset` so you are back on main.
Write only the SHA — no extra words. Do not rewrite main.
problemStatement.overview: Sprint Service health check (`./check.sh`) fails on today's `main` but passed at v1.0. Jordan forgot to pin the single bad commit — find its SHA so she can revert just that change.
problemStatement.brief: Between v1.0 (good) and main (bad), find the single first commit that makes `./check.sh` fail. Write its SHA to `~/answers/bad-commit`.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Bisect the Broken Board Status Check

`./check.sh` is the Sprint Service health check. It fails on today's `main` but still passed at tag `v1.0`. Jordan is sure exactly one commit spilled the break; find that first bad SHA with bisect instead of reading ~18 commits by hand.

## 1. Reproduce

```bash
cd ~/sprint-service
./check.sh                 # FAIL on today's main
git tag                    # v1.0 = last known good
```

## 2. Bisect (automated)

```bash
git bisect start
git bisect bad                 # HEAD is broken
git bisect good v1.0           # v1.0 was fine
git bisect run ./check.sh
```

After a few automatic checkouts Git prints `<sha> is the first bad commit`.

## Manual alternative

```bash
git bisect start
git bisect bad
git bisect good v1.0
./check.sh && git bisect good || git bisect bad   # repeat until Git announces the culprit
```

## 3. Record and clean up

```bash
git rev-parse refs/bisect/bad > ~/answers/bad-commit
git bisect reset
git branch --show-current    # main
```

## Why it is fast

With ~18 candidates and a single breaker, bisect needs at most a handful of `./check.sh` runs instead of reading every commit.
